items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: I don't know who named it after Fred Robbins, the disk jockey there...

ctx.x: They had been together I guess about two or three months. And right after I left Billy Eckstine as his accompanist, about three weeks later, in early 1948, I think about the last week in January, I got this call from Illinois. He was going into the Apollo Theatre, and he needed a pianist. I asked him what had happened to Sir Charles -- because I knew Sir Charles. He said that Sir Charles had quit. So I needed a job and the money was good, he was offering me good money -- so I went and joined the band.

I got there and I found out Sir Charles had quit because of a misunderstanding that he had with Illinois over a tune that he had written called "Robbins Nest." It seems as if Illinois had recorded the tune, and I don't know who named it after Fred Robbins, the disk jockey there... So they called it "Robbins Nest."
